thread:
Mira P.: heads up — got a customer (acct: acme-ops) reporting intermittent p99 spikes after the continuous-batching change we rolled last night. spikes are ~600-900ms above baseline, p95 looks okay. filing here before paging.
Alex K.: thanks — can you paste the sample request + region + model? any correlation with sequence length?
Mira P.: model: redwood-llama-13b-v2 (cpu fallback disabled), region: us-west-2, request sample: ~200 tokens average, some >1024. Customer says spike happens ~1-2x per 1000 requests.
Samir: pinging oncall. @oncall-bot can you pull the last 2 hours of pod metrics for the dedicated pool serving that model? cpu/gpu util, batch sizes, and batch wait_ms.
oncall-bot: fetching metrics for pool: redwood-dedicated-usw2-13b (2h)... attaching summary link: https://grafana.example/r/dedicated-pool/1812345678
Priya (runtime): quick thought — this sounds like the batch handoff issue we saw in feb where tiny batches linger because of max_wait_ms being too aggressive. what was the max_wait_ms in the deploy?
Mira P.: config on the fleet: \n```\ncontinuous_batching: true\nmax_batch_size: 64\nmax_wait_ms: 8\nmin_batch_size: 8\nenable_kv_cache: true\n```\nThat's the same config we rolled.
Alex K.: max_wait_ms=8 is pretty low; that favors latency but can cause more tiny-batch handoffs if traffic isn't steady. Could explain p95 fine but p99 spikes when a request waits for the tail of a batch.
Samir: attaching a truncated log excerpt when spike occurred:\n```\n[2026-03-15T02:12:06Z] request_id=abcd batch_wait=7ms batch_size=3 handoff=true exec_start=2026-03-15T02:12:06.123Z exec_end=2026-03-15T02:12:06.998Z total=875ms\n[2026-03-15T02:12:06Z] model_kernel_switch=quantized->fp16 cache_miss=true\n```\nNote the kernel switch + cache miss — that can amplify a tiny batch cost.
Priya (runtime): aha; kernel warmup + cache miss are multiplicative. Tiny-batch handoffs reduce amortization of kernel setup. That log matches a 3-item batch where one request waited only ~7ms to be sent out but then hit a cold path.
Devex Jen: customer-facing note: we should propose a mitigation quickly: bump max_wait_ms to 25ms and lower max_batch_size to 48 for that pool as a temporary canary. That should reduce exaggerated p99s with minimal p95 impact. Also propose adding a routing policy to prefer larger batch windows for >512 token requests.
Mira P.: can we do that as a canary on 10% of the pool? we need low-risk change.
Alex K.: yes — i'll prepare a canary patch: change config for 2 of the 20 nodes in the pool. steps:\n1) update fleet config for nodes n-03 and n-07\n2) monitor p50/p95/p99 and GPU util for 30 minutes\n3) rollback if p99 doesn't improve or latency elsewhere regresses\n
Samir: I'll watch the logs. Also adding a temporary rule to avoid model kernel switches mid-batch: prefer homogeneous kernel-packed batches for 13b if possible. That requires a runtime tweak; @Priya can you advise on feasibility?
Priya (runtime): we can add a heuristic: if a batch contains both cached and cache-miss requests we prefer to wait up to an extra 15ms to coalesce, but it's a small runtime change — want to avoid a full deploy. For now we can add a dispatcher flag to prefer coalescing for the affected shard.
Mira P.: what's the immediate mitigation timeline? customer is pushing for response.
Alex K.: canary rollout will be done in ~20 mins. I'll post a summary when it's live. action items -> I'll create a short runbook for SRE ops to flip the two nodes and monitoring alerts.
Devex Jen: writing a customer note: "we've identified batching handoffs combined with kernel warmups as the likely root cause. We are rolling a low-risk canary that increases batching window for a small subset of your traffic — this reduces tail latency for long-context requests while maintaining normal median latency. Will update in 30m."
Samir: can we add a synthetic replay that mimics the customer's token distribution? I'll run a local load test against the canary nodes.
Priya (runtime): also enabling additional debug logging for 10 minutes on the canary nodes to capture batch composition and kernel switch events: will post logs.
oncall-bot: canary config applied to nodes n-03,n-07 at 2026-03-15T02:32:10Z (operator: alexk). Monitoring started.
Alex K.: canary results after 30m: p99 for affected customer dropped from +850ms to +120ms. p95 unchanged. GPU util on canary nodes increased by ~6% but within headroom. rolling to 30% with same config.
Mira P.: customer updated: "baseline improved, thanks — still seeing rare hiccups but much better". should we keep increased window permanently?
Priya (runtime): suggest longer A/B: 24-48h run with updated config, plus adding the dispatcher heuristic as a follow-up. also add a metric for kernel_switch_count per-batch so we can alert earlier.
Alex K.: filing ticket INF-7842 for runtime heuristic and metric work. We'll also add a short KB for customer-facing explanation.
Mira P.: closing loop: customer is satisfied with the canary results; keeping monitoring. summary posted to the incident channel later. :thumbsup:
